title: Wi-Fi
subtitle: Every visible network around you — live signal, security, channel, and the access point behind it.
emptyDesc: Run a scan to list every Wi-Fi network in range. Scanning may require Location access on macOS.
scanningDesc: Sweeping the radio for nearby networks, signal levels, and security details.
noRadioDesc: This machine has no wireless radio Clarity can read, so there is nothing to scan.
radioOffDesc: Switch the wireless radio on and rescan to see the networks around you.
locationBannerBody: macOS hides each access point's BSSID and country code from apps without Location Services access. Network names are already visible — grant access to reveal the rest.
locationOpenSettings: If nothing changes, enable Location Services for Clarity in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services.
locationOpenSettingsHint: Opening System Settings — enable Location Services for Clarity, then rescan.
hiddenExplainer: A hidden network simply leaves its name out of the beacon — it isn't a security measure. Most of the hidden networks around you belong to hardware you already own: the service SSIDs consumer routers ship with, and the backhaul links mesh nodes use to talk to each other. The access point's manufacturer and its signal strength are what tell them apart: −34 dBm is a device in the same room, −70 dBm is somebody else's.
demoModeHint: Mask every network name and BSSID so a screenshot is safe to share. Country codes stay visible — they aren't identifying.
detailEmpty: Select a network to inspect its details and live signal.
noLongerVisible: This network is no longer visible.
